title: Stage 2: Services and the database
summary: Give the API a stable address and run PostgreSQL with its own disk.

steps.title: Two Services and a StatefulSet
body: ports: [{ port: 80, targetPort: http }]      # 'http' is the named containerPort 8080
clusterIP: None                               # headless: db-0.db.shop resolves to the pod
The API reaches the database at `db-0.db.shop.svc.cluster.local:5432` (or simply `db:5432` from inside `shop`).

steps.prompt: What is the PVC created for `db-0` called?
steps.explain: `<template name>-<statefulset name>-<ordinal>`. It survives the pod and is reattached when `db-0` is recreated.

steps.prompt: The API pods are labelled `app: shop-api` and listen on the named port `http` (8080). Complete the Service.
steps.explain: The API stays internal; stage 5's Ingress is the only way in from outside.

items: other pods call the API at a stable name
traffic only goes to ready API pods
`db-0.db.shop` resolves to the database pod's IP
the database keeps its disk when the pod moves
the database pod is always called `db-0`

steps.title: Check the wiring
prompt: Write `List<string> Wiring(List<(string Name, Dictionary<string, string> Selector, string TargetPort)> services, List<(string Name, Dictionary<string, string> Labels, Dictionary<string, int> Ports)> pods)`.
For each Service, in order, return one line:
- no pod matches its selector: `"NAME: no pods match selector"`
- pods match, but `TargetPort` is neither a port **name** in the pod's `Ports` nor a port **number** (as text) among its values: `"NAME: targetPort T not found on POD"` (first matching pod)
- otherwise `"NAME: N pods"` (number of matching pods)
starter: List<string> Wiring(List<(string Name, Dictionary<string, string> Selector, string TargetPort)> services,
List<(string Name, Dictionary<string, string> Labels, Dictionary<string, int> Ports)> pods)
solution: List<string> Wiring(List<(string Name, Dictionary<string, string> Selector, string TargetPort)> services,
List<(string Name, Dictionary<string, string> Labels, Dictionary<string, int> Ports)> pods)
var matching = pods.Where(p => s.Selector.Count > 0 && s.Selector.All(kv => p.Labels.TryGetValue(kv.Key, out var v) && v == kv.Value)).ToList();
if (matching.Count == 0) { lines.Add($"{s.Name}: no pods match selector"); continue; }
if (bad.Name is not null) { lines.Add($"{s.Name}: targetPort {s.TargetPort} not found on {bad.Name}"); continue; }
template: var dojoPods = new List<(string Name, Dictionary<string, string> Labels, Dictionary<string, int> Ports)> {
Dojo.Eq("stage manifests", new List<string> { "shop-api: 2 pods", "db: 1 pods" },
Dojo.Eq("typo in selector", new List<string> { "api: no pods match selector" }, Wiring(new() { ("api", new() { ["app"] = "shopapi" }, "http") }, dojoPods));
Dojo.Eq("wrong port", new List<string> { "shop-api: targetPort 80 not found on shop-api-a" }, Wiring(new() { ("shop-api", new() { ["app"] = "shop-api" }, "80") }, dojoPods));
Dojo.Eq("number works too", new List<string> { "shop-api: 2 pods" }, Wiring(new() { ("shop-api", new() { ["app"] = "shop-api" }, "8080") }, dojoPods));
hints: Reuse your selector matching; an empty selector matches nothing for a Service.
A tuple from `FirstOrDefault` has `Name == null` when nothing was found.
